questions.q: What was Yahweh’s command to Aaron about the seven lamps?
questions.a: Yahweh commanded that the lamps must give light in front of the lampstand.

questions.q: Who showed Moses the pattern for the lamp?
questions.a: Yahweh showed Moses the pattern for the lamp.

questions.q: What did Yahweh ask Moses do to the Levites?
questions.a: Yahweh told Moses to take the Levites from among the people of Israel and purify them.

questions.q: What did Moses do to the Levites to purify them?
questions.a: Moses sprinkled them with water of atonement, shaved their entire bodies, and washed their clothes.

questions.q: What was the offering that the Levites brought?
questions.a: The Levites brought two young bulls and a grain offering with fine flour mixed with oil.

questions.q: What did Yahweh tell Moses to ask the people of Israel to do to the Levites to purify them?
questions.a: Yahweh told the people of Israel to lay their hands on the Levites.

questions.q: Why did they present the Levites as though they were raised high before Yaweh?
questions.a: They presented the Levites on behalf of the people so that the Levites might serve Yahweh.

questions.q: What kinds of offerings were the bulls for the Levites?
questions.a: The bulls were a sin offering and a burnt offering to atone for the Levites.

questions.q: Where did the Levites place their hands?
questions.a: The Levites placed their hands on the heads of the bulls.

questions.q: What tribe was separated, purified, and lifted up as an offering to Yahweh so they could serve in the tent of meeting?
questions.a: The Levite tribe was separated, purified, and lifted up as an offering to Yahweh so they could serve in the tent of meeting.

questions.q: When did Yahweh set apart all the firstborn people and animals for himself?
questions.a: Yahweh set apart all the firstborn of people and animals for himself since the day he took the lives of all the firstborn of the Egyptians in the land of Egypt.

questions.q: Whom did Yahweh give to the people of Israel to atone for the people so that no plague would harm them when they came near the sanctuary?
questions.a: He gave the Levites, instead of the firstborn, to Aaron and his sons to do the work and to atone for the people in the tent of meeting.

questions.q: Did Moses, Aaron, and the whole community do everything that Yahweh had commanded concerning Levites?
questions.a: Yes, they did everything that Yahweh had commanded Moses concerning the Levites.

questions.q: What did Yahweh say to Moses about the age limits of serving in the tent meeting?
questions.a: Levites who were twenty-five years old could serve until they were fifty years.

questions.q: What could they do when they could not serve in the tabernacle after 50?
questions.a: Levites after 50 years old could help their brothers.

commentary.text: Consecration of the Levites, and their service.

Verses 1–4 Aaron himself lighted the lamps, thus representing his Divine Master. The Scripture is a light shining in a dark place, 2Pe 1:19. A dark place even the church would be without it; as the tabernacle, which had no window, would have been without the lamps. The work of ministers is to light these lamps, by expounding and applying the word of God. Jesus Christ is the only Light of our dark, sinful world; and by his atonement, by his word and the Holy Spirit, he diffuses light around.

Here we have directions for the solemn ordination of the Levites. All Israel must know that they took not this honour to themselves, but were called of God to it; nor was it enough that they were distinguished from others. All who are employed for God, must be dedicated to him, according to the employment. Christians must be baptized, ministers must be ordained; we must first give ourselves unto the Lord, and then our services. The Levites must be cleansed. They must be clean that bear the vessels of the Lord. Moses must sprinkle the water of purifying upon them. This signifies the application of the blood of Christ to our souls by faith, that we may be fit to serve the living God. God declares his acceptance of them. All who expect to share in the privileges of the tabernacle, must resolve to do the service of the tabernacle. As, on the one hand, none of God's creatures are his necessary servants, he needs not the service of any of them; so none are merely honorary servants, to do nothing. All whom God owns, he employs; angels themselves have their services.
